{"status": "Excellent", "grammar_rule": "Verbs like gustar: indirect object + verb + subject", "explanation": "You correctly used 'me encanta' with the subject 'la comida espanola' — the verb agrees with the thing that delights (la comida, singular). Your sentence is natural and grammatically perfect.", "correction": null, "b1_alternative": null, "c1_alternative": "Soy un apasionado de la gastronomia espanola; en particular, la paella valenciana me resulta exquisita.", "tip": null}

{"status": "Excellent", "grammar_rule": "Type 3 Si clause: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, result + conditional perfect", "explanation": "This is a flawless Type 3 conditional expressing an impossible past condition. 'Hubiera sabido' (pluperfect subjunctive) and 'habria aceptado' (conditional perfect) create the past counterfactual perfectly. The vocabulary is professional and the register is appropriate for C1.", "correction": null, "b1_alternative": "No sabia la verdad. No acepte el trabajo.", "c1_alternative": null, "tip": null}

The learner is at level B2. Analyze this Spanish sentence: "Me gustaria saber si pudieras ayudarme con este proyecto."

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Si meaning 'whether/if' takes indicative, not subjunctive", "explanation": "When 'si' means 'whether' (indirect question), it takes the indicative: 'si puedes' or 'si podrias'. The subjunctive 'pudieras' after 'si' is only used in hypothetical Type 2 conditions (si pudieras = if you could). Here you're asking whether someone can help, not posing a hypothetical.", "correction": "Me gustaria saber si podrias ayudarme con este proyecto.", "b1_alternative": "Puedes ayudarme con este proyecto?", "c1_alternative": "Desearia consultarle si le seria posible brindarme su colaboracion en este proyecto.", "tip": "Two meanings of 'si': (1) 'if' (hypothetical condition) takes imperfect subjunctive; (2) 'whether' (indirect question) takes indicative or conditional."}

{"status": "Excellent", "grammar_rule": "Imperfect subjunctive in indirect commands (sequence of tenses)", "explanation": "After 'dijo que' (a past-tense verb of commanding/requesting), you correctly shifted to the imperfect subjunctive 'estudiaramos'. This shows strong command of the sequence of tenses, which is a key B2 skill. A common error would be using the present subjunctive 'estudiemos' instead.", "correction": null, "b1_alternative": "El profesor dijo: 'Estudien para el examen.'", "c1_alternative": "El catedratico nos exhorto a prepararnos exhaustivamente de cara al examen del viernes.", "tip": null}

The learner is at level B1. Analyze this Spanish sentence: "Yo he ido al supermercado esta manana y compre muchas frutas."

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Mixing preterite perfecto and indefinido in the same time frame", "explanation": "You started with the present perfect 'he ido' (appropriate with 'esta manana' in peninsular Spanish), but then switched to the preterite 'compre'. Within the same time frame, you should be consistent. Either use both in present perfect or both in preterite.", "correction": "He ido al supermercado esta manana y he comprado muchas frutas.", "b1_alternative": null, "c1_alternative": "Esta manana me he acercado al supermercado y he adquirido una buena variedad de fruta.", "tip": "In Spain, use preterito perfecto for 'today' time frames (esta manana, hoy, esta semana). In Latin America, preterito indefinido is preferred even for recent events."}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Gender agreement: 'problema' is masculine despite ending in -a", "explanation": "'Problema' is one of the Greek-origin words ending in -ma that are masculine in Spanish. The correct article is 'el problema', not 'la problema'. This is a very common B1 error.", "correction": "El problema es que no tenemos suficiente dinero.", "b1_alternative": null, "c1_alternative": "El inconveniente radica en la insuficiencia de fondos.", "tip": "Other masculine -ma words: el tema, el sistema, el programa, el idioma, el clima, el dilema. Memorize these as a group."}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Anglicism: 'hacer una llamada de telefono' calques English 'make a phone call'", "explanation": "While 'hacer una llamada' is acceptable, 'llamada de telefono' is redundant and sounds like a direct translation from English. In natural Spanish, you simply say 'llamar por telefono' or just 'llamar'.", "correction": "Necesito llamar a mi madre por telefono.", "b1_alternative": "Necesito llamar a mi mama.", "c1_alternative": "Debo ponerme en contacto telefonico con mi madre.", "tip": "Simpler is more natural in Spanish. Instead of 'hacer una reservacion' (Anglicism), say 'reservar'. Instead of 'tomar una decision', say 'decidir' or 'tomar una decision' (not 'hacer')."}

{"status": "Excellent", "grammar_rule": "'Antes de que' + imperfect subjunctive with pluperfect in the main clause", "explanation": "'Antes de que' always triggers the subjunctive, and since the action is in the past, you correctly used the imperfect subjunctive 'llegaramos'. The pluperfect 'habia despegado' correctly establishes the earlier-than-past timeline. This is a clean B2 construction.", "correction": null, "b1_alternative": "Llegamos tarde. El avion ya salio.", "c1_alternative": "Antes de nuestra llegada al aeropuerto, la aeronave ya habia emprendido el vuelo.", "tip": null}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Anglicism: 'aplicar para' is an English calque of 'apply for'", "explanation": "'Aplicar para un trabajo' is a direct translation from English. In Spanish, the correct expression is 'solicitar un empleo' or 'postularse para un puesto'. This Anglicism is extremely common among English-speaking learners and immediately marks speech as non-native.", "correction": "Necesito solicitar un empleo nuevo en esta empresa.", "b1_alternative": "Quiero buscar un trabajo nuevo.", "c1_alternative": "Debo presentar mi candidatura para un nuevo puesto en esta empresa.", "tip": "Common Anglicisms to avoid: 'aplicar para' (use solicitar), 'realizar' for 'to realize' (use darse cuenta), 'soportar' for 'to support' (use apoyar), 'atender' for 'to attend' (use asistir a)."}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Ser vs Estar for temporary states — Estar with adjectives describing conditions", "explanation": "You correctly chose 'estar' for a temporary condition (being tired), which is good! However, 'estuve' (preterite) implies the tiredness is a completed event. Since you're describing your state/condition after work, the imperfect 'estaba' is more natural — it sets the background scene.", "correction": "Ayer yo estaba muy cansado despues del trabajo.", "b1_alternative": null, "c1_alternative": "Ayer me encontraba agotado tras la jornada laboral.", "tip": "Use imperfect for states and conditions in the past (estaba cansado, tenia hambre, hacia frio). Use preterite for actions that happened (comi, sali, llegue)."}

This is one of the most common ser/estar errors.", "correction": "Yo estoy de acuerdo con tu opinion sobre este tema.", "b1_alternative": null, "c1_alternative": "Coincido plenamente con tu postura respecto a este asunto.", "tip": "Fixed expressions with estar: estar de acuerdo, estar de vacaciones, estar de pie, estar de moda, estar de buen/mal humor."}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Subjunctive mood after 'querer que'", "explanation": "After 'querer que' with two different subjects, Spanish requires the subjunctive. 'Vienes' is the present indicative — it must be 'vengas' (present subjunctive). This is the most fundamental subjunctive trigger at B2.", "correction": "Yo quiero que tu vengas conmigo al mercado.", "b1_alternative": "Quiero ir contigo al mercado.", "c1_alternative": "Me gustaria que me acompanaras al mercado.", "tip": "Remember the WEIRDO triggers: Wishes, Emotions, Impersonal expressions, Recommendations, Doubt, Ojala. 'Querer que' is a Wish."}

{"status": "Needs Improvement", "grammar_rule": "Anglicism: 'realizarse' does not mean 'to realize' in the sense of becoming aware", "explanation": "'Realizar' means 'to carry out/accomplish' in Spanish, not 'to realize/become aware'. This is a false cognate and one of the most common Anglicisms. The correct verb is 'darse cuenta de que'.", "correction": "Ella se ha dado cuenta de que estaba equivocada.", "b1_alternative": "Ella sabe que estaba equivocada.", "c1_alternative": "Ha cobrado conciencia de su error.", "tip": "False cognates to watch: realizar (accomplish, not realize), actualmente (currently, not actually), sensible (sensitive, not sensible), exito (success, not exit)."}
